review.note: A15(4): the record was dated {"start":1814,"end":1814,"date":"1814-10-02"} and the first sentence of the cited article states "on October 1, 1814, to October 2, 1814", so the day bounds are 1814-10-01 to 1814-10-02. The years are unchanged. Deviation 1534: that clause is the month-first mirror of the crossing shape and datesInLead read only its opening day, so the range was reported as a contradiction instead of the gap it is.

title: Battle of Rancagua
summary: The English Wikipedia article "Battle of Rancagua", at revision 1371210959, opens: "The Battle of Rancagua, also known in Chile as the Disaster of Rancagua, occurred on October 1, 1814, to October 2, 1814, when the Spanish Army under the command of Mariano Osorio defeated the Chilean forces led by Bernardo O’Higgins. This put an end to the Chilean Patria Vieja and it was the decisive step of the Spanish military Reconquest of Chile." That is the article's account and not yet this atlas's; nobody has read this record, and review.html is where somebody does. Wikidata item Q1310755, imported by tools/import/wikidata.mjs. The item's own description reads "1814 battle". Everything here is copied from the item's own fields and nothing in it is this atlas's account of the thing: that is still to be written, and review.html is where somebody writes it.
